absent: Numeric values of audit class tags and operation markers plus full contents of generic audit header lists.
Platform assignment of the Simple Boot Flag port and behavior when the port is absent or concurrently accessed.
Byte pattern and relocation rules of the call thunk template plus exclusion logic and setup steps.
Exact encoding of fine branch control flow checks and reporting paths for integrity failures.
Trap frame layout and return path details for control protection faults beyond dispatch.
Definition and lifecycle of the delayed work object used for periodic low memory scans.
ACRN frequency helper results and hypervisor callback protocol beyond handler invocation.
Model specific register numbers and side effects for AMD configuration adjustments not shown in the visible part.

findings.text: Audit classification entry points distinguish 32-bit compatibility architecture from native execution and map open family plus execution requests to dedicated audit operation types, falling back to a native marker for other numbers.
All five audit class tables are terminated by an all-ones unsigned sentinel that delimits the variable length list supplied by generic headers.

Early initialization registers native read, write, directory write, attribute change and signal class tables, and when 32-bit emulation is enabled also registers the corresponding compatibility tables, always reporting success.
Simple Boot Flag byte uses bit zero for plug-and-play OS, bit one for booting, bit two for diagnostics, bit seven for parity, and a reserved mask of hex 78 covering the remaining middle bits.
Simple Boot Flag port accesses hold the lock named rtc_lock with interrupt state preserved across the critical section, applied symmetrically to reads and writes.
A Simple Boot Flag value counts as valid only when no reserved bits are set and its parity is odd in the sense checked by the helper, otherwise setup emits a warning about invalid stored content.

Simple Boot Flag setup moves from unconfigured to active by reading the stored byte, warning if invalid, clearing reserved plus booting plus diagnostic positions, optionally asserting plug-and-play OS, then writing back with parity adjustment.

Call thunk patching limits a single patch to 254 bytes and aligns detection to the configured function alignment boundary, with template size derived from the distance between template start and tail symbols.

A core text range descriptor carries a start address, an end address and a name reference, instantiated once for built in kernel text bounded by linker symbols and per module from its text memory base plus size and name.
Four per CPU 64-bit counters track call thunks, returns, stuffing operations and context switches, exposed read only through debug filesystem snapshots.
A kernel command line switch enables call thunk debugging by setting a flag that persists for built in or module use and always reports successful parsing.
Module call site patching serializes setup work with the lock named text_mutex, skipping entirely when thunk support has not finished initializing.
A location counts as a call thunk only after initialization completes, after skipping excluded addresses, and after its preceding padding bytes match a relocated copy of the template.

Accounting emission appends a relocated template copy at the supplied program position and advances the pointer by the template length, emitting nothing when uninitialized or when the call target itself is already a thunk.
Debug filesystem setup creates a top directory plus one per possible CPU file with owner read write and others read only access, each file rendering the four counters for its CPU on read.

Control protection error encoding masks the low fifteen bits for cause, with values one through five for near return, far return or interrupt return, missing endbranch, restore supervisor shadow stack, and set busy, plus the top bit of the low sixteen marking enclave origin.
Control protection cause strings are looked up by masked error value with out of range values folded to an unknown entry, avoiding out of bounds access.
Unexpected control protection faults log a one time warning distinguishing user mode from kernel mode and naming the decoded cause, without terminating the faulting context at that point.

User control protection handling reads the user shadow stack pointer before re enabling interrupts, records error and trap number in the current thread, emits a rate limited diagnostic with instruction pointer, stack pointer, shadow stack pointer and enclave indication, then forces a segmentation fault with control protection code and disables interrupts again.

Kernel control protection handling treats only missing endbranch as expected, tolerates a known self test address by clearing the result register and wait for event flag, otherwise either warns and clears the flag in non fatal mode or halts. Boot options select disabled versus warning versus default fatal behavior.

The control protection exception entry dispatches on privilege level and feature enablement, routing user faults to user handling only when user shadow stacks are active and kernel faults to kernel handling only when indirect branch tracking is active, otherwise using the unexpected path.

Control flow integrity failure decoding reads twelve then six bytes backwards from the faulting address, expects two specific opcode families, derives the expected type as the negation of an immediate field and the target from a register selected by addressing bits, failing closed on copy or decode errors.

Control flow integrity dispatch branches on global mode, validating trap location with a one byte adjustment for an updated sequence in kernel control flow mode, delegating to a separate fine branch decoder in fine mode, and reporting no trap for unknown modes or decode failures.

Low memory corruption checking allows at most eight scan areas, defaults the scan size to sixty four kibibytes and the period to sixty seconds, and uses negative one to mean decide at setup from build configuration.
A scan area descriptor pairs a sixty four bit physical address with a sixty four bit length, stored in a fixed array with a separate count of populated entries.

Three early command line parsers configure the corruption check enable flag, period in seconds and size with suffix parsing, each rejecting missing arguments and propagating numeric conversion failures.

Low memory setup resolves the tri state enable, disables on zero size, rounds the size up to page granularity, then walks free memory ranges clamped to the low region, reserving and zeroing each qualifying range until the area table fills.

Periodic low memory validation scans recorded areas word by word, logs physical location and offending value for any non zero entry, clears it, and raises a one time warning if any corruption was observed.
A delayed work handler re arms itself with period converted to clock ticks and rounded for coalescing, started immediately only when areas exist, checking is enabled and the period is non zero.
ACRN guest support detects the hypervisor through a CPU identifier helper, installs a system vector handler for hypervisor callbacks and points time calibration hooks at a shared frequency helper.
The ACRN callback entry always acknowledges the local interrupt controller before accounting and optional handler invocation, preserving and restoring the previous interrupt register context.
ACRN callback dispatch calls a registered function pointer only when non null, with separate install and remove operations that store or clear the pointer without synchronization shown.
The ACRN hypervisor descriptor provides a name, a detection routine, a type tag and initialization callbacks for platform setup and extended interrupt addressing availability.
ACRN extended interrupt addressing support directly reflects whether the boot processor reports the corresponding feature.
Legacy AMD register access authorizes safe operations with a fixed key of hex 9c5a203a and warns when the boot processor family differs from fifteen.
A read only after init sixteen bit limit for batched global invalidate operations defaults to one.
On 32-bit builds specific early AMD models clear an aliased configuration space enable to avoid later driver interference with processor speed control.
Elan configuration base uses address hex fffc with an enable bit at position thirty one and a key of hex cb.

Early AMD K6 setup applies model and stepping specific workarounds including feature flag adjustments, a timing loop stability assessment, and sized write allocation enablement bounded to five hundred eight megabytes for old style and four thousand ninety two megabytes for new style, serialized by cache flush under disabled interrupts.

Early AMD K7 setup enables disabled vector support through hardware configuration bit fifteen for models six through ten, reprograms clock control high bits to hex two for model eight stepping one and above, and restricts symmetric multiprocessing certification to selected model and stepping combinations.
A padding table provides thirty two single byte no operation encodings for code alignment use.
Two compilation units define distinct informational log prefixes for call thunk diagnostics and for low memory checking respectively.
